title: CoralTemp v3.1 has mean steps at the 1995 ATSR-2 and 2002 AATSR starts, in 2008 and in 2020; removing them cuts 2024 reef pixels at DHW 4 or more from 83% to 63% (35S-35N, six references)
abstract: Question: is CoralTemp v3.1, the daily SST record behind NOAA Coral Reef Watch (CRW) bleaching alerts, homogeneous, and do its changes alter the reported reef heat stress? Approach: we compared CoralTemp at 35S-35N (1985-2025) with six references of different types (ERSSTv5, HadSST4.2, mean-homogenised DOISST, ESA SST CCI v3 without in situ data, 97 moored buoys, 1,662 reef pixels), searched for breaks with ENSO terms, fitted smoothed step fields, removed them and recalculated the CRW MMM climatology, Degree Heating Months (1985-2025) and daily Degree Heating Weeks (2023-2025). Results: all references show the same staircase: June 1995 (-0.04 to -0.16 C), August 2002 (+0.06 to +0.12 C), January 2008 (+0.04 to +0.07 C) and about October 2020 (+0.04 to +0.06 C). At daily resolution the first two steps fall on 21 May-30 June 1995 and 19 July-4 August 2002, at the starts of ATSR-2 and AATSR data and not at the documented November 2002 merge (merge term -0.02 to +0.03 C). The steps explain all of the CoralTemp warming excess: +0.031 to +0.039 C per decade against the references (+0.049 at the reef pixels; GTMBA buoys +0.012). The homogenised MMM is 0.14 C higher (0.128-0.141 for all variants, including a satellite-only one); our recalculation of the official MMM agrees within 0.004 C. The 1985-2025 trend of annual maximum Degree Heating Months falls by about 20% (ratio 0.78-0.82). In 2024, reef pixels at DHW >= 4 C-weeks fall from 83.1% (official; 82.8% recalculated) to 62.9% (61-67% for six variants), and at DHW >= 8 from 51.2% to 36.9%; for 2023-2025, pixels at DHW >= 4 in any year fall from 90.6% to 73.4%. Limitations: the references have their own errors and share some inputs; break dates were chosen from the data; causes are inferred, not confirmed; the fields are smoothed over 1000 km; noise changes were not corrected; daily DHW covers only 2023-2025; the reef pixels are coral-survey cells, not the CRW reef mask.

display.caption: CoralTemp v3.1 minus six references (12-month means) and joint step-model estimates: the same steps in June 1995, August 2002, January 2008 and about October 2020 against in situ, satellite-only and buoy references; the documented 2016 splice is small.
Daily-resolution view (every eighth day): the 1995 and 2002 steps coincide with the ATSR-2 (31 May 1995) and AATSR (23 July 2002) data starts, not with the November 2002 OSTIA-to-Geo-Polar merge.

Consequences at 1,662 reef pixels: MMM change after homogenisation (mean +0.14 C), annual maximum Degree Heating Months 1985-2025, and the share of reef pixels at DHW >= 4 and >= 8 C-weeks in 2023-2025 (official, recomputed and homogenised).
